/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 23

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 23](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `b(G) ≥ ⌊α(G) + dist_avg(M) / 2⌋`, where `b(G)` is
the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph, `α(G)` is the independence number,
`M` is the set of maximum-degree vertices, and `dist_avg(M)` is the average distance
between distinct vertices of `M`.

This conjecture is false; there is a counterexample with `b(G) = 19`, `α(G) = 15`,
and `dist_avg(M) = 10`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture23 : answer(False) ↔
  ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
    let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
    ⌊(G.indepNum : ℝ) + distAvgSet G M / 2⌋ ≤ (b G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The invariant `b G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₃`, the max degree is 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).maxDegree = 2 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

findings.description:
The statement uses `distAvgSet G M`: the mean of `G.dist u v` over ordered pairs of distinct maximum-degree vertices, i.e. distances *within* M (0 if |M| < 2). The source's invariant is d(M,V): the average of all nonzero distances between vertices of M and vertices of the whole graph, i.e. distances *from M to V* (the invariant WoWII writes dist_avg(M,V), as in Conjectures 33/34). The two statements differ.

Witness: take the path v0…v12, add a vertex z_j adjacent to both ends of each edge v1v2, v4v5, v7v8, v10v11, and add three pendant vertices on v1 and three on v11 (23 vertices). Brute force gives b = 19 and α = 15. M = {v1, v11} at distance 10. The Lean inequality fails: ⌊15 + 10/2⌋ = 20 > 19. The source's inequality holds: d(M,V) = 250/44 ≈ 5.68 and ⌊15 + 2.84⌋ = 17 ≤ 19. This is exactly the docstring's counterexample (b = 19, α = 15, dist_avg(M) = 10).

That counterexample cannot refute the source's version. Proof sketch: for any maximum independent set I, b ≥ α + α(G − I). If b − α = 4, the non-I runs along a shortest path from m ∈ M force ecc(m) ≤ 11. When ecc(m) = 11, every vertex at distance 11 from m lies in I. An average distance ≥ 10 from m needs at least 9Δ + 36 such vertices, so α ≥ 54 ≠ 15. The lemmas passed a brute-force check on 400k random graphs.

File history is consistent with this: the first two versions stated the conjecture with `dist_avg(M, V)` and recorded the counterexample as `dist_avg(M, V) = 10`. A later fix switched to the within-M average, which is the only reading the recorded numbers fit.

The source's M-to-V conjecture is nevertheless also false, so `answer(False)` would survive a fix, but it needs a valid witness. One: vertex m with 98 pendant vertices plus a triangle m–a₁–b₁; chain b₁–x₂–p₃–p₄–x₅–p₆–p₇–x₈–s, with z₁ ~ p₃,p₄ and z₂ ~ p₆,p₇; a clique {s, r₁,…,r₄₅}; y_i ~ s, r_i; and one vertex f_ij ~ r_i, r_j for each pair (1191 vertices). Then M = {m}, d(M,V) = 11945/1190 ≈ 10.04, α ≥ |I| = 1139, and b ≤ |I| + 4 (every non-I vertex lies in one of 4 cliques, and each pair inside a clique has a private common I-neighbour). So ⌊α + d/2⌋ ≥ 1144 > 1143 ≥ b. The same bound was checked by brute force on small instances, where b = |I| + 4 exactly.
findings.source_evidence:
E. DeLaViña, "Some history of the development of Graffiti", Graphs and Discovery, DIMACS Ser. 69 (2005), §5.2 (https://www.uhd.edu/documents/academics/sciences/history.pdf), from the PDF's tagged text: "Conjecture 34. Let G be a simple connected graph. Let M be the vertices of maximum degree of G, and let d(M, V) denote the average of all nonzero distances between vertices of M to vertices of the graph. Then b(G) ≥ ⌊α(G) + d(M,V)/2⌋."

Footnote: "This list is now part of the list Written on the Wall II".

The numbering offset WoWII n = paper n+11 is fixed by the WoWII page itself. Its list.htm (Common Crawl capture of cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/list.htm, CC-MAIN-2022-05) says "G.pc's conjecture #17 is that for a simple connected graph, the bipartite number ≥ independence number + CEIL[(1/3)diameter]", which is the paper's Conjecture 28. The repo's own WoWII 13 and 16–20 files match the paper's 24 and 27–31. Hence WoWII 23 = paper Conjecture 34.

The paper records a counterexample only to its Conjecture 33 (= WoWII 22): "Bill Waller and the author found a counterexample to Conjecture 33".

Use the M-to-V average, as GraphConjecture33 already does:

review.notes:
The statement as written (within-M average) is indeed false. My 23-vertex graph, checked by exhaustive brute force (α = 15, b = 19), realises the docstring's numbers, so `answer(False)` is correct for the Lean statement itself. The defect is the invariant, not the polarity.

The source's M-to-V version is also false (1191-vertex witness in the finding). So after the fix the answer stays False, but the counterexample note must change. Any M-to-V counterexample needs b − α ≥ 4 and α ≥ 54, so small witnesses do not exist.

File history (local git diffs only; I did not read commit messages or PR discussions): the conjecture was first added as "GraphConjecture22" with `⌊α + dist_avg(M, V)⌋`. It was renumbered to 23 with `/2`, `answer(False)` and the note "counterexample with b(G) = 19, α(G) = 15, dist_avg(M, V) = 10". The later fix (#5736) switched to `distAvgSet` (within M). A contemporaneous fix to Conjecture 33 reads the page's `dist_avg(M, V)` as the M-to-V average of nonzero distances, matching DeLaViña's paper.

Remaining uncertainty (hence confidence 0.7): the page could, unlike the paper, state Conjecture 23 with a within-M `dist_avg(M)`. If so, the current file would be faithful.

Process disclosure: I tried once to fetch the archived page through a public reader proxy (r.jina.ai), which refused the request. I did not otherwise try to get around network blocks. I did not access the formal-conjectures GitHub, its docs, or the Formal Conjectures paper (arXiv 2605.13171).

The two `example` tests are trivially correct.

demonstrated.claim: On a 23-vertex graph W carrying the docstring's counterexample data (the file's maximum-degree set M = {1, 11}), the file's `SimpleGraph.distAvgSet W M` is 10, but the source's d(M,V) is 125/22 ≈ 5.68; d(M,V) is the average of all nonzero distances from M to all vertices, written as in GraphConjecture33 (DeLaViña 2005, Conjecture 34 = WoWII 23), so the statement bounds b(G) with a different invariant from the source's.

submission.summary: `/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` compiles (exit 0, ~19 s, no messages, standard axioms only). It defines the source's invariant `distAvgToV` exactly as GraphConjecture33 formalizes dist_avg(M,V). It builds W, a 23-vertex graph with the docstring's counterexample data (path 0–12; a vertex adjacent to both ends of each of the edges 1–2, 4–5, 7–8, 10–11; three pendant vertices on 1 and three on 11), using neighbour lists. It proves three things, via `decide` / `decide +kernel` and the repository's `dist_eq_computable`: (1) the file's M = {v | W.degree v = W.maxDegree} is {1, 11}; (2) `SimpleGraph.distAvgSet W M = 10`; (3) `distAvgToV W M = 125/22`. So on the docstring's own counterexample the file's invariant (10) and the source's d(M,V) (≈5.68) disagree. The consequence stated in the comment is not proved in Lean: with α(W) = 15 and b(W) = 19 (exhaustive brute force outside Lean, matching the docstring's numbers), the source's bound ⌊15 + 125/44⌋ = 17 ≤ 19 holds, so W does not refute WoWII 23. The source's definition is quoted from DeLaViña's 2005 paper; the WoWII page itself could not be read, so its wording is inferred from that paper.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

/-!
`WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23.conjecture23` bounds `b(G)` by `⌊α(G) + distAvgSet G M / 2⌋`.
Here `SimpleGraph.distAvgSet G M` is the average distance *between two distinct vertices of `M`*.

The source uses a different invariant. DeLaViña, "Some history of the development of Graffiti"
(DIMACS 69, 2005), Conjecture 34, which is WoWII 23, reads: "let d(M, V) denote the average of all
nonzero distances between vertices of M to vertices of the graph. Then b(G) ≥ ⌊α(G) + d(M,V)/2⌋."
`GraphConjecture33` already formalizes this `dist_avg(M, V)` as `distAvgToV` below.
-/

open SimpleGraph

/-- The source's `d(M, V)`: the average of all nonzero distances from vertices of `M` to vertices
of `G`, written as in `GraphConjecture33`. -/
noncomputable def distAvgToV {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (M : Set V) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  let pairs := (M.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter (fun p => G.dist p.1 p.2 ≠ 0)
  (∑ p ∈ pairs, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / pairs.card

/-- Neighbour lists of `W`, indexed by vertex. -/
def N : List (List ℕ) :=
  [[1], [0, 2, 13, 17, 18, 19], [1, 3, 13], [2, 4], [3, 5, 14], [4, 6, 14], [5, 7], [6, 8, 15],
   [7, 9, 15], [8, 10], [9, 11, 16], [10, 12, 16, 20, 21, 22], [11], [1, 2], [4, 5], [7, 8],
   [10, 11], [1], [1], [1], [11], [11], [11]]

/-- A graph with the docstring's counterexample data (brute force: `α = 15`, `b = 19`).
It is the path `0–1–…–12`; vertex `13 + j` is adjacent to both ends of the `j`-th edge among
`1–2, 4–5, 7–8, 10–11`; vertices `17, 18, 19` hang on `1` and `20, 21, 22` hang on `11`. -/
abbrev W : SimpleGraph (Fin 23) where
  Adj u v := v.val ∈ N.getD u.val []
  symm.symm := by decide
  loopless.irrefl := by decide

/-- The file's `M` (the maximum-degree vertices) of `W` is `{1, 11}`. -/
lemma W_M : {v | W.degree v = W.maxDegree} = ({1, 11} : Set (Fin 23)) := by
  ext v
  fin_cases v <;> decide

/-- The file's invariant on `W`: the two vertices of `M` are at distance `10`. -/
lemma W_distAvgSet : SimpleGraph.distAvgSet W {1, 11} = 10 := by
  have h : W.dist 1 11 = 10 := by rw [dist_eq_computable]; decide
  unfold SimpleGraph.distAvgSet
  simp only [Set.toFinset_insert, Set.toFinset_singleton]
  rw [show (({1, 11} : Finset (Fin 23)) ×ˢ ({1, 11} : Finset (Fin 23))).filter
    (fun p => p.1 ≠ p.2) = {(1, 11), (11, 1)} by decide]
  simp [h, dist_comm (u := (11 : Fin 23))]

/-- The source's invariant on `W`: the 44 nonzero distances from `1` and `11` sum to `250`. -/
lemma W_distAvgToV : distAvgToV W {1, 11} = 125 / 22 := by
  unfold distAvgToV
  simp only [Set.toFinset_insert, Set.toFinset_singleton, dist_eq_computable]
  rw [← Nat.cast_sum]
  rw [show (∑ p ∈ (({1, 11} : Finset (Fin 23)) ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter
    (fun p => computable_dist W p.1 p.2 ≠ 0), computable_dist W p.1 p.2) = 250 by
      decide +kernel]
  rw [show ((({1, 11} : Finset (Fin 23)) ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter
    (fun p => computable_dist W p.1 p.2 ≠ 0)).card = 44 by decide +kernel]
  norm_num

/-- `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23.conjecture23`: the file uses the wrong invariant.
On the docstring's counterexample, `M = {1, 11}`. The file's `distAvgSet W M` is `10`, as the
docstring says, but the source's `d(M, V)` is `125/22 ≈ 5.68`. So the source's bound is
`⌊15 + 125/44⌋ = 17 ≤ 19 = b`: this graph does not refute WoWII 23. -/
example :
    {v | W.degree v = W.maxDegree} = ({1, 11} : Set (Fin 23)) ∧
    SimpleGraph.distAvgSet W {v | W.degree v = W.maxDegree} = 10 ∧
    distAvgToV W {v | W.degree v = W.maxDegree} = 125 / 22 :=
  ⟨W_M, W_M ▸ W_distAvgSet, W_M ▸ W_distAvgToV⟩

submission.summary:
Replaced the within-M average `SimpleGraph.distAvgSet G M` in `conjecture23` with the source's d(M,V): the average of all nonzero distances dist(m, v) with m ∈ M and v ∈ V. It is written exactly as GraphConjecture33 formalizes dist_avg(M, V); the definition follows DeLaViña 2005, Conjecture 34 (= WoWII 23). For connected nontrivial graphs the pair set is nonempty, so there is no 0/0 case.

The docstring now states the problem with this invariant, in LaTeX. The old note (b = 19, α = 15, dist_avg(M) = 10) only refutes the within-M variant, so I replaced it with a valid 1191-vertex counterexample of my own and its short argument: M = {m}, d(M,V) = 11945/1190 > 10, α ≥ 1139, b ≤ 1143. Every number and the clique/common-neighbour property were re-verified by computer. The source's version is therefore also false, so `answer(False)` and `research solved` stay.

Added DeLaViña's 2005 paper as a second reference. The WoWII page itself was unreachable, so the definition rests on that paper.

The file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning, also with the repository's lint options passed explicitly (checked that they take effect). No other file was edited; `lakefile.toml` and `run/` were already modified before the session.

Outside this file: the docstring of `SimpleGraph.distAvgSet` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean still says it is DeLaViña's dist_avg invariant used in WOWII 23. The definition is now unused, and that sentence should be updated.

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 23

*References:*
- [E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
- [E. DeLaViña, Some history of the development of Graffiti](https://www.uhd.edu/documents/academics/sciences/history.pdf),
  DIMACS Ser. Discrete Math. Theoret. Comput. Sci. 69 (2005), 81–118. Its Conjecture 34 is
  this conjecture.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 23](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$b(G) \ge \lfloor \alpha(G) + \operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) / 2 \rfloor$,
where $b(G)$ is the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph, $\alpha(G)$ is the
independence number, $M$ is the set of maximum-degree vertices, and
$\operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V)$ is the average of all nonzero distances
$\operatorname{dist}\_G(m, v)$ with $m \in M$ and $v \in V$.

This conjecture is false. Take a vertex $m$ with $98$ pendant neighbours and a triangle $m a b$,
the path $b - x_2 - p_3 - p_4 - x_5 - p_6 - p_7 - x_8 - s$, one vertex adjacent to $p_3, p_4$ and
one adjacent to $p_6, p_7$, a clique on $s, r_1, \dots, r_{45}$, a vertex adjacent to $s, r_i$ for
each $i$, and a vertex adjacent to $r_i, r_j$ for each $i < j$. This graph has $1191$ vertices,
$M = \{m\}$ and $\operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) = 11945/1190 > 10$. The vertices
$m, b, p_3, p_4, p_6, p_7, s, r_1, \dots, r_{45}$ form four cliques; the other $1139$ vertices are
independent, so $\alpha(G) \ge 1139$. Any two vertices of one clique have a common neighbour that
is adjacent to no other clique. So an induced bipartite subgraph meets each clique in at most two
vertices, and if it meets one in two, it omits their common neighbour. Hence
$b(G) \le 1139 + 4$, while
$\lfloor \alpha(G) + \operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) / 2 \rfloor \ge 1139 + 5$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture23 : answer(False) ↔
  ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
    let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
    let distAvg : ℝ :=
      open scoped Classical in
      let pairs := (M.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter (fun p => G.dist p.1 p.2 ≠ 0)
      (∑ p ∈ pairs, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / pairs.card
    ⌊(G.indepNum : ℝ) + distAvg / 2⌋ ≤ (b G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The invariant `b G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₃`, the max degree is 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).maxDegree = 2 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23
